title: How a moral panic forms
researchPrompt: Explain the stages by which a society comes to treat something as an urgent threat out of proportion to the evidence, and why the pattern repeats across unrelated subjects.
suggestedAngles: Walk the sequence: a trigger, amplification, a folk devil, then policy that outlives the panic
Focus on the incentives of each actor rather than blaming any one of them
Use the aftermath to show how the response persists after the fear fades

title: Schelling's segregation model
researchPrompt: Explain how a population where nobody wants segregation can still end up sharply segregated, and what that implies about inferring intent from outcomes.
suggestedAngles: Run the grid mentally: a mild preference, applied repeatedly, cascades
Separate individual intent from aggregate outcome as distinct levels of explanation
Draw the uncomfortable corollary: fixing the outcome may need more than fixing attitudes

title: Preference falsification and sudden collapse
researchPrompt: Explain why regimes and social norms that look stable can collapse almost overnight, and why nobody sees it coming - including the people who wanted it.
suggestedAngles: Distinguish private belief from public preference, and make the gap the mechanism
Use revolutionary thresholds to explain why the cascade is discontinuous
Confront the prediction problem: the hidden distribution is unobservable by construction

references.label: Kuran (1991) — Now Out of Never: The Element of Surprise in the East European Revolution
